items.heading: Amendment to BMC Chapter 2.99 to Establish Surveillance Technology Vendor Accountability Requirements and to Revise the Annual Surveillance Technology Reporting Schedule
items.action: Action: Adopted first reading of Ordinance No. 8,033–N.S. revised to amend Section 4 of the ordinance to read as follows: 2.99.070 Oversight Following City Council Approval. The City Manager must submit to the Council Action Calendar a written Surveillance Technology Report, covering all of the City’s Surveillance Technologies, annually at the first regular Council meeting in March. Each Surveillance Technology Report shall cover the preceding calendar year, January 1 through December 31. The first March Surveillance Technology Report submitted following the effective date of the ordinance amending this Section shall be submitted at the first regular Council meeting in March 2028 and shall cover the period from October 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027, so that no period is omitted from annual reporting as a result of the transition to a calendar-year reporting period. After review of the Surveillance Technology Report, Council may make modifications to Surveillance Use Policies. Second reading scheduled for October 13, 2026.

items.heading: Adoption of San Pablo Avenue Specific Plan
items.action: Action: M/S/C (Blackaby/Kesarwani) to suspend the rules and extend the Council meeting to 11:30 p.m. Vote: All Ayes. Action Calendar – Public Hearings Action: M/S/Failed (Blackaby/O’Keefe) to: 1. Adopt a Resolution as revised in Supplemental Communications Packet #1 by the City Manager. 2. Adopt the first reading of an Ordinance as revised in the Supplemental Communications Packet #1 by the City Manager and further revised as follows: • In Section 9 of the ordinance, amend Table 23.204-45: C-SP Development Standards to amend the Main Building Height Maximum to 55 ft. and 4 stories for non-residential project land use and 55 ft. and 5 stories for residential only or mixed-use project land use. • Add a Minimum Density Standard of 100 Dwellings Units Per Acre (dua) and amend all references to 145 dua in the Supplemental packet to 100 dua. • In Section 9 of the ordinance, amend the language in 23.204.160(D)(3)(c); related to Prohibited Uses on the Ground Floor to change “Prohibited Uses” to “Residential Uses.” • In Section 16 of the ordinance, amend 23.206.080(B)(6) to read as follows: 6. Affordable and Family Housing Opportunity Areas. To increase affordable housing production and expand the supply of family-sized units, the MU-LI district shall include an Affordable and Family Housing Opportunity Area as shown in Figure 23.206-1. Multi-unit and mixed-use residential uses shall be allowed within the Affordable and Family Housing Opportunity Area with a UP(PH), provided that the development project either: a) Offers 100 percent of the residential units, excluding any manager’s unit, at a rent that is affordable to households earning no more than 120 percent of the Area Median Income (AMI) with at least 50 percent earning no more than 80 percent AMI; or b) Provides at least 35 percent of the residential units as either two- or three- bedroom units. 3. Refer to the City Manager consideration of the application, within the context of the San Pablo Area Specific Plan, San Pablo Avenue Specific Plan Design Standards Document, and/or any associated documents, as applicable, of commercial anti-displacement provisions being considered as part of the Commercial Zoning Update and provisions of the RENAISSANCE 1 and RENAISSANCE 2 referrals previously adopted by the Berkeley City Council. These could include, but not be limited to, the evaluation of a business license tax waiver for businesses displaced by developmental projects; establishment of marketing and promotional programs to boost activity to impacted businesses, facilitated by the Office of Economic Development and community partners; facilitation of meetings between construction project managers and impacted nearby businesses to identify potential accommodations; creation of development standards that include the warm-shelling of new commercial spaces; and identification of additional mitigation measures or policy changes/waivers to support business continuity and relocation. Vote: Ayes – O’Keefe, Blackaby; Noes – Kesarwani, Taplin, Bartlett, Tregub, Lunaparra, Humbert, Ishii; Abstain – None; Absent – None. Action Calendar – Public Hearings Action: M/S/Carried (Kesarwani/Taplin) to: 1. Adopt Resolution No. 72,466–N.S. as revised in Supplemental Communications Packet #1 by the City Manager. 2. Adopt the first reading of Ordinance No. 8,034–N.S. as revised in the Supplemental Communications Packet #1 by the City Manager and further revised as follows: • In Section 9 of the ordinance, amend Table 23.204-45: C-SP Development Standards to amend the Main Building Height Maximum to 75 ft. and 5 stories for non-residential project land use. • Add a Minimum Density Standard of 100 Dwellings Units Per Acre (dua) and amend all references to 145 dua in the Supplemental packet to 100 dua. • In Section 9 of the ordinance amend the language in 23.204.160(D)(3)(c); related to Prohibited Uses on the Ground Floor to change “Prohibited Uses” to “Residential Uses.” • In Section 16 of the ordinance, amend 23.206.080(B)(6) to read as follows: 6. Affordable and Family Housing Opportunity Areas. To increase affordable housing production and expand the supply of family-sized units, the MU-LI district shall include an Affordable and Family Housing Opportunity Area as shown in Figure 23.206-1. Multi-unit and mixed-use residential uses shall be allowed within the Affordable and Family Housing Opportunity Area with a UP(PH), provided that the development project either: a) Offers 100 percent of the residential units, excluding any manager’s unit, at a rent that is affordable to households earning no more than 120 percent of the Area Median Income (AMI) with at least 50 percent earning no more than 80 percent AMI; or b) Provides at least 35 percent of the residential units as either two- or three- bedroom units. Second reading scheduled for October 13, 2026. 3. Refer to the City Manager consideration of the application, within the context of the San Pablo Area Specific Plan, San Pablo Avenue Specific Plan Design Standards Document, and/or any associated documents, as applicable, of commercial anti-displacement provisions being considered as part of the Commercial Zoning Update and provisions of the RENAISSANCE 1 and RENAISSANCE 2 referrals previously adopted by the Berkeley City Council. These could include, but not be limited to, the evaluation of a business license tax waiver for businesses displaced by developmental projects; establishment of marketing and promotional programs to boost activity to impacted businesses, facilitated by the Office of Economic Development and community partners; facilitation of meetings between construction project managers and impacted nearby businesses to identify potential accommodations; creation of development standards that include the warm-shelling of new commercial spaces; and identification of additional mitigation measures or policy changes/waivers to support business continuity and relocation. Vote: All Ayes.
